hooks.text: Until Pioneer 10, no craft crossed the asteroid belt or reached Jupiter.
Pioneer 10 was the first spacecraft to reach our solar system's escape velocity.
One nuclear probe was the first to travel past the asteroid belt.

title: Pioneer 10: The First Scout to Jupiter
description: In 1972, Pioneer 10 became the first spacecraft to navigate the asteroid belt and reach Jupiter, carrying a golden message into the deep.

beats.text: Until Pioneer 10, no craft crossed the asteroid belt or reached Jupiter.
beats.visual: NASA artist concept of Pioneer 10 approaching Jupiter, 1972

beats.text: In 1972, NASA's Pioneer 10 became the first nuclear-powered probe to attempt the journey.
beats.visual: photograph of Pioneer 10 launching on Atlas-Centaur rocket, March 1972

beats.text: It survived intense radiation that triggered false commands while passing within 82,000 miles of Jupiter.
beats.visual: Pioneer 10 photograph of Jupiter and the Great Red Spot, 1973

beats.text: On its hull, a gold-anodized plaque showed two human figures and a map of 14 pulsars.
beats.visual: official NASA photograph of the Pioneer 10 gold-anodized plaque, 1972

beats.text: After passing Neptune's orbit in 1983, it became the first craft to head for interstellar space.
beats.visual: NASA diagram showing Pioneer 10 trajectory past Neptune into deep space

beats.text: But navigators noticed a mysterious, tiny drag on its signal called the Pioneer Anomaly.
beats.visual: Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex antenna at night, 2000

beats.text: Later analysis revealed it wasn't new physics, but just heat escaping unevenly from the probe.
beats.visual: technical diagram of thermal recoil radiation causing the Pioneer Anomaly, 2012

beats.text: Now drifting toward Aldebaran, it ventured where
beats.visual: telescope image of the red giant star Aldebaran in constellation Taurus
